scenario: A 5-year-old male with asthma presents with worsening cough, wheeze, and shortness of breath. The case involves severe pediatric asthma that fails initial therapy, progresses to fatigue, requires intubation, and may develop post-intubation hypotension, hypoxia, and bradycardia if respiratory mechanics are not addressed.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's start a nebulized salbutamol treatment now — he's wheezy and tight, working hard to breathe.

messages.content: Yeah, I use puffers at home. And it felt hard to breathe like this before. My chest still feels all tight and I'm scared.

messages.content: Give IV magnesium sulfate now — he's still tight and working hard despite the nebs and steroid.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a venous blood gas now — I want to see his CO2 and how much he's tiring out after maximal therapy.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Venous gas back: pH 7.21, pCO2 75, pO2 55, HCO3 20, lactate 3.7. He's tiring — CO2's high and he's acidotic. Still HR 182, RR 36, BP 68/44, sat 95 on NRB at 0.8.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: He's failing maximal therapy — gas shows pCO2 75 and pH 7.21, and he's tiring. Prepare for RSI and intubation now: set up for BVM preoxygenation and draw up induction and paralytic.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, BVM in place with good pre-oxygenation. Suction and tube confirmed at bedside, ready for intubation on your go.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: He's dropped to 55/36 after intubation — positive-pressure is cutting his preload. Push a 250 mL normal saline bolus now, that's 10 mL/kg for 25 kg.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get a post-intubation chest X-ray now — I need to confirm the tube position and rule out a pneumothorax given his BP is still 67/42 on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give a second 250 mL normal saline bolus now — another 10 mL/kg. He's still hypotensive at 60/38 and satting only 89% on the vent. And disconnect him briefly to let him fully exhale — watch for breath-stacking and auto-PEEP with his asthma.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start an epinephrine infusion now — he's still hypotensive after two saline boluses, this is fluid-refractory. Titrate to perfusion.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Epi infusion running and titrating. BP's come up to 93/55, HR 171, sat 91% on the vent. Post-intubation chest X-ray is back — tube position normal, no pneumothorax.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Repeat the venous blood gas now — I need to see if his CO2 and acidosis are improving post-intubation so I can adjust the vent settings.
